Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

various adjective

also varied, all sorts of, all kinds of, diverse, for various reasons

classical

Cic. Sen. 46: variō sermōne
Plin. Ep. 9.36.4: variīs sermōnibus
Traupman 401

varius, varia, varium

adjective

various, of different kinds; varied

Talk of all sorts is varius sermō. For various reasons is multīs dē causīs (Caes. BG 4.16; Traupman 106, 369).

Other words

  • dīversus, dīversa, dīversum — different, of different kinds; going different ways

    also used · classical · Catull. 46.10–11: dīversae variē viae; Col. 12.47.6: dīversa genera

    Stronger than varius: things set apart from one another (see different).

  • complūrēs, complūra — several, a number of

    adjective, third declension, plural only; neuter also complūria (mostly early Latin) · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 2.2.22: mulierēs complūrēs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 10.6.3: complūrēs cōnsulēs (Lewis & Short)

    For “various” meaning “several”, with no stress on their being different.

Examples

  • convīviumque vīcīnōrum cotīdiē compleō, quod ad multam noctem quam maximē possumus variō sermōne prōdūcimus

    every day I fill my table with neighbours, and we draw the evening out as far into the night as we can with talk of every kindCic. Sen. 46

  • ita variīs sermōnibus vespera extenditur, et quamquam longissimus diēs bene conditur

    so the evening is drawn out with talk of various kinds, and even the longest day is well laid to restPlin. Ep. 9.36.4

See also different, kind.
